en: Therīgāthā 6.8 Chakkanipāta Vijayātherīgāthā Vijayā, the Elder Nun I am now free from all suffering; I have reached the state of peace. I have crossed over the flood; I have attained the further shore. I have seen the Dhamma that is well-taught by the One Well-Gone. I have realized Nibbāna through direct knowledge. I have no fear of death; I have no longing for life. I abide with an even mind, having abandoned both. My mind is liberated, well-liberated by means of wisdom. I have attained the destruction of all taints. I have no more birth; my existence is brought to an end. I have lived the holy life; there is nothing further to do. “Four times and five times I went forth from my dwelling;
not having attained peace of mind, I left.”
Lacking mastery over my own mind,
I approached a bhikkhunī and questioned her respectfully.
She taught me the Dhamma:
the elements and the sense-bases,
and the Four Noble Truths.
The faculties and the powers;
the factors of enlightenment and the eightfold path,
for the attainment of the supreme goal.
Having heard his words,
I acted according to his instruction;
during the first watch of the night,
I recollected my previous births.
In the middle watch of the night,
I purified the divine eye.
In the last watch of the night,
I shattered the mass of darkness.
And with rapture and bliss, my body—
Dwelling there, having split it asunder,
on the seventh day I extended my foot,
having shattered the mass of darkness.
… The Elder Nun Vijayā … The Sixth Chapter is finished.
